A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoG work. Their main text, Appendices A–E, equations, six tables and 24 figures are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original graph-construction experiments, oracle comparisons and ablations in Tables 2–5, plus additional backbone results and case studies in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the main comparisons, ablations and Appendix E evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same context module, augmentation actions, guided generation, oracle selection and AutoG variants. No algorithm or prompt procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight datasets in Table 1 and Appendix B, with the same downstream tasks. The synthetic MAG-derived tests with original and anonymous column names are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains XGBoost, DeepFM, TabGNN, vanilla and JTD schemas with R2N/R2NE, and expert schemas. Comparator membership in the oracle, ablation and additional-backbone experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The GNN and LLM settings, evaluation metrics and column-renaming control remain unchanged. Section 4.3 retains the same oracle evaluation design, including 30% sampling and the early metric at 10% of training epochs.

E4.justification: The generation/oracle ablations in Table 4, prompt-component and anonymous-column analyses in Table 5, and Appendix E's LLM comparisons and schema case studies are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point-estimate tables without seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Section 4.4's description of repeated candidate generation is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and rankings in Tables 2–6, along with the qualitative appendix findings, are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports MovieLens AUC values of 69.10 for AutoG and 69.73 for the expert schema in both versions.

T1.justification: The tabular-data and heterogeneous-graph definitions in Section 2 and Appendix A are unchanged apart from spacing. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: formalizing graph construction through benchmarks and proposing AutoG, with performance approaching human-designed schemas. Their scope and qualifications are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix E retain the same interpretations and limitations concerning column-name semantics, harmful relationships, weak network effects and LLM backbone failures. Repositioned case-study paragraphs contain no new explanations.

D1.justification: The code-access information, dataset descriptions, complete Appendix D prompts and action documentation, and schema-construction details remain unchanged. Appendix reflow does not add or remove reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 6, Appendix C and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. References shifting between pages are not citation additions or removals.

P1.justification: Section 8 removes the funding acknowledgment for Zhikai Chen and Jiliang Tang, including NSF, ARO and corporate support, while retaining thanks to the 4DBInfer authors. Otherwise, changes are limited to spacing and the version/date stamp; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All tables and figures retain their content and structure. Minor spacing and page reflow alter appendix placement: for example, the E.3.1–E.3.2 explanations move from page 30 to page 28 while their schema figures remain on page 30.

improvement.justification: The methods, evidence, claims, limitations and reproducibility material are unchanged, including the appendices. Removing the funding acknowledgment reduces disclosure detail, while the spacing and reflow offer no substantive improvement; these limited changes do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
